entries.title: KEY TELEPORT
entries.body: Coldcard feature that allows the encrypted transfer of confidential data between two devices. Transferable data includes *seeds* (main *seed* or *Seed Vault*), notes and passwords, full backups, and multisig PSBTs.

entries.title: KEYNESIANISM
entries.body:
School of economic thought based on the work of the British economist John Maynard Keynes. Keynesianism advocates active state intervention in the economy to stabilize economic cycles. Keynesian policies rely on the ability of central banks to adjust the money supply and interest rates, as well as on the ability of governments to borrow and spend. This theoretical framework largely dominates contemporary economic policy.

In the Bitcoin community, Keynesianism is often criticized. Bitcoiners, who are generally close to the Austrian school, criticize it for encouraging monetary expansion, distorting price signals through the manipulation of interest rates, promoting malinvestment, and generating growing public debt. Bitcoin, with its fixed supply and the impossibility of manipulating it monetarily, is fundamentally incompatible with Keynesian monetary policy tools.

entries.title: KEYSEND
entries.body:
Payment method on the Lightning Network that allows funds to be sent directly to a node's public key, without the recipient needing to generate an invoice beforehand. Unlike the classic BOLT-11 flow where the recipient chooses the preimage and passes it along via the invoice, here the sender generates the preimage and includes it in the payment's encrypted onion packet. Only the recipient node can decrypt the packet and retrieve the preimage to finalize the HTLC.

The recipient node must explicitly enable keysend reception (`accept-keysend=true` in the LND configuration). Arbitrary data can be attached to the payment via TLV records, which makes keysend useful for donations, streaming payments (Podcasting 2.0), or messaging between nodes. The main limitation is the absence of proof of payment: since the sender chooses the preimage themselves, they cannot prove after the fact that they made the payment.

entries.title: KEYSTORE
entries.body: In the context of Bitcoin wallet software, a keystore is a structure that groups together the information needed to track and use a set of keys. It generally contains a label, a master key fingerprint (*master fingerprint*), a derivation path, and an extended public key (`xpub`). These elements allow the wallet to generate receiving addresses and monitor the transactions associated with them.

entries.title: KNAPSACK SOLVER
entries.body: Former method used for coin selection in the Bitcoin Core wallet before version 0.17. The *Knapsack Solver* attempts to solve the coin selection problem by iteratively and randomly choosing UTXOs, and adding them up in subsets, with the aim of minimizing fees and the size of the transaction. This method has since been replaced by *Branch-and-Bound*.

entries.title: KRUX
entries.body: Open source firmware that turns Kendryte K210 microcontroller devices, such as the Maix Amigo or the M5StickV, into Bitcoin transaction signing devices. Krux makes it possible to generate and manage private keys, sign transactions offline, and interact with coordinator wallets (Sparrow, Specter...) via QR codes or microSD cards. The project is aimed at users who want to build a low-cost *hardware wallet* from generic off-the-shelf hardware, while retaining full control over the source code.
